components.name: AccentBar
components.title: AccentBar
components.summary: A thin 3px progress line filled with the signature gradient, available as the React `AccentBar` and as `.cr-accentbar` classes.
whenToUse: Use for quiet, passive progress: how far through a chapter, an audio teaching, a reading plan or an onboarding carousel.
Use on dark surfaces by default (app player, `.sec-ink` bands); use `.cr-accentbar-light` on white or `--off-white`.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for uploads, form steps or anything the user waits on; use Progress for that.
Do not use as a decorative rule; use Divider (`.thread`).

anatomy.description: A track (18% white on dark, 12% black on light) with a gradient fill from the left. No labels, no handle.
anatomy.markup: The HTML bar fills its parent's width; set a width on the parent, not on the bar.

props.name: progress
props.description: Fraction filled, 0 to 1.

props.name: width
props.description: Track width in px, or any CSS width such as "100%".

props.name: light
props.description: Light track (`rgba(0,0,0,.12)`) for white or off-white surfaces. The default track is for dark surfaces.

props.name: label
props.description:
Accessible name ("John 3 read"). When given, the track gets `role="progressbar"` with value attributes.
Without it the bar is plain divs: show the value in text beside it.

props.description:
Gradient view such as `LinearGradient` from expo-linear-gradient or react-native-linear-gradient. The fill is `gradient-signature`.

variantNotes: States: empty (0%), partial, complete (100%). The fill is always `--gradient-signature`; it never changes colour for "done".

rules: Fill with `--gradient-signature` only. Never solid Horizon Blue (`--horizon-blue`); blue is reserved for the one primary button.
Keep it 3px tall with a 2px radius. Do not thicken it into a progress bar.

Pair it with a nearby text value when the number matters ("9:12 left", "Day 4 of 21").
Do not animate it on load; update it as real progress changes.

components.name: Accordion
components.title: Accordion
components.summary: The FAQ accordion: rounded, bordered rows built on native `<details>`/`<summary>` that open in place with a plus that turns to a cross.
whenToUse: Use for FAQs and other sets of short, independent answers people scan by question.
Use on the FAQ page, at the foot of product pages (dot.Bible app, NFC cards, HD Radio) and in giving help.
whenNotToUse: Do not hide content everyone needs (prices, key steps, legal terms people must read); show it.
Do not nest accordions or put forms inside one.

anatomy.description: The row styles (`.acc`, `details`, `summary`, `.ans`) come from the base layer; `.dp-acc-panel` adds the optional `--gray-100` panel.

props.name: items
props.description: The rows.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled list of open item ids. Several rows may be open at once.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Uncontrolled initial open ids. Open the first row by default on the FAQ page only; elsewhere start all closed.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the open ids when a row opens or closes.

props.name: panel
props.description: Place the rows on the `--gray-100` panel. Drop it to sit straight on the page.

variantNotes: Closed: white row, `--border-hairline-light` border, `--radius-ml` corners, 30px circular plus on the right.
Open: border turns to 45% Horizon Blue, the plus rotates 45° into a cross, answer shows below in `--gray-700` 16px.
Hover: pointer cursor on the summary; no colour change.
Focus: `summary:focus-visible` gets the Horizon Blue outline and `--shadow-focus`.
Panel: `.dp-acc-panel` places the rows on a `--gray-100` card with `--radius-lg` and 24px padding.

states.universal: See rules/states.md for the seven required states and their hooks.

rules: The caret/plus means "opens here". Never use ↗ or › on an accordion row.
Open the first item by default on the FAQ page only; elsewhere start all closed.
Several rows may be open at once; do not force exclusive opening.
Keep 12px between rows (`.acc` gap). Summary row is at least 44px tall.
Put links inside answers in `--horizon-blue`; links to another page end in ↗.
Do not add icons or numbers before the question.

components.name: Alert
components.title: Alert
components.summary: Inline status banners (info, success, warning, error) that sit in the page flow, plus the dismissible dark announcement bar that sits above the header.
whenToUse: Use an inline alert to report the state of the thing right below it: a form result, a gift that failed, a card about to expire.
Use the announcement bar for one site-wide message, such as a launch or a broadcast milestone.
whenNotToUse: Do not use an alert for a passing confirmation after an action; use a Toast.
Do not use an alert to ask a question or block the page; use a Modal.
Do not stack more than two alerts. Merge the messages or fix the cause.

anatomy.description: Status icon + bold title + one sentence + optional link. Classes `.alert` and `.alert-*` come from the base layer; `.fb-alert` adds the titled layout.

props.name: variant
props.description: Status. Never restyle colours per page; use one of the four variants.

props.name: title
props.description: Bold title that says what happened in plain words. Omit for the compact one-line form.

props.name: children
props.description: One sentence that says what to do next, with at most one text link (use `<a className="fb-alert-link">`).

props.name: compact
props.description: One-line form without a title, for example a draft notice.

props.name: role
props.description:
Live-region role. Defaults to `alert` for errors (announced at once) and `status` for the other variants.
Insert the alert into the DOM when the event happens; a pre-rendered hidden alert is not announced.

props.name: variant
props.description: Status. Never restyle colours per screen.

props.name: title
props.description: Bold title saying what happened. Omit for a compact one-line alert.

props.name: children
props.description: The sentence that says what to do next.

props.name: link
props.type: { label: string; onPress: () => void; accessibilityHint?: string }
props.description: At most one text link (no buttons inside an alert).

props.name: compact
props.description: One line, no title, 14dp text.

variants.colours: one line, e.g. a draft notice

states.universal: See rules/states.md for the seven required states and their hooks.

rules: Radius `--radius-md` (12px), padding 16px 18px, 1px status `-line` border. Never restyle colours per page; use the four status variants.
Text 15px, title 16px/600 (`.fb-alert-title`). Links use `.fb-alert-link`: inherit the status colour, weight 600.
Put the alert directly above the content it describes. After a form submit, move it to the top of the form.
Icon: 20px inline SVG, stroke currentColor, 1.8 width, round caps. Info = circle-i, success = circle-check, warning = triangle, error = circle-!.
Do not put buttons inside an inline alert. One text link at most.
Link icons: ↗ when the link goes to another page; no icon when it only scrolls or edits here.
The announcement bar is 48px min-height, 15px text, dark `--charcoal-900`. Show one at a time. Full-bleed above the header uses `.fb-announce-flush` (square corners).
The bar's close is `.fb-x`, a 44px round button. Remember the dismissal for the visit (sessionStorage); do not show it again on the next page.
Never use red for anything except errors. Counts and new-item dots are Horizon Blue.

components.name: AnchorNav
components.title: AnchorNav
components.summary: In-page links for long pages: a sticky "On this page" list beside the content on desktop, and a horizontal sticky anchor bar under the header for product pages and phones.
whenToUse: Use the side list (`.nv-otp`) on long reading pages with 4+ sections: Statement of Faith, Privacy, Terms, Cookie Policy.
Use the anchor bar (`.nv-abar`) on product pages (dot.Bible App, ISM Radio, NFC Cards) and on every long page below 1024px.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it on short pages with fewer than 4 sections.
Do not use it to switch content in place; that is Tabs. Anchor links scroll to sections that are all on the page.

anatomy.description: Lay the side list out in a two-column grid: `240px` list, `minmax(0,1fr)` content, 64px gap.

props.name: items
props.description: The sections, in page order. Maximum 8.

props.name: variant
props.description: `side` is the sticky "On this page" list for long reading pages; `bar` is the sticky horizontal bar under the header.

props.name: heading
props.description: Visible heading of the side list ("On this page"). Side variant only.

props.name: title
props.description: Product name at the start of the bar ("dot.Bible App"). Bar variant only.

props.name: action
props.description: Optional single action at the end of the bar, for example a `btn btn-primary btn-sm` link. Bar variant only.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the `<nav>`.

props.name: current
props.description: Id of the active section (controlled). When omitted the active section follows the scroll position.

props.name: onCurrentChange
props.description: Called when the section in view changes.

props.name: linkComponent
props.description:
Component used to render links. Defaults to `'a'`.
Pass `next/link` (or any component accepting `href`, `className`, `onClick`, `aria-current` and `children`).

props.name: scrollOffset
props.description: Height in px of the sticky offset used by the scroll spy (header plus bar).

variantNotes: **Side list item:** 40px rows, 15px `var(--gray-700)` on a 2px `var(--gray-200)` rail.
Hover: text `var(--black)`.
Active (the section in view): `aria-current="true"`, `var(--horizon-blue-dim)` 600 and a `var(--horizon-blue)` rail segment.
Focus: blue outline + `var(--shadow-focus)`.
**Side list position:** `.nv-otp-wrap` is `position:sticky; top:96px` (72px header + 24px).

**Anchor bar:** 60px white bar, `position:sticky; top:72px`, `var(--gray-200)` bottom hairline. Links 15px/500; active is 600 with a 2px `var(--horizon-blue)` underline. Add `.nv-stuck` once it sticks to show the soft shadow.
**Anchor bar action:** optional single `.btn-primary .btn-sm` on the right ("Get the app").
**Below 1024px:** hide the side list; use the bar. Links scroll sideways, never wrap.

rules: Set the active item from scroll position (IntersectionObserver), not on click alone.
Only one item is active at a time.
Keep labels identical to the section headings they point to.
The bar's button is the one Horizon Blue primary in that view. Leave it out when the page hero already has a blue primary in view.
Give every section `scroll-margin-top` of 96px (side list) or 140px (bar) so headings are not hidden under the sticky header.
Never use ↗ or › in anchor links; they stay on this page.
Max 8 items in either form.

components.name: AppBanner
components.title: AppBanner
components.summary: Promotes the dot.Bible app in three sizes: a dismissible "Open in app" smart banner on mobile, an inline promo card with QR and store badges on desktop, and a slim strip at the end of an article.
whenToUse: Smart banner `.mn-sbanner`: top of mobile pages on dot.bible and ism.bible, once per visit.
Promo card `.mn-promo`: inside a page section about the app or Scripture access.
Slim strip `.mn-strip`: end of an article or reading page.
whenNotToUse: Do not stack more than one app promotion in a view.
Do not use for giving or newsletter asks; use DonationWidget or NewsletterCard.

components.name: AppBar
components.title: AppBar
components.summary: The top bar of a mobile app screen: status bar, a 56px row with back, title and icon actions, and an optional large title or search field.
whenToUse: Use at the top of every screen in ISM apps such as dot.Bible.
Use the large title on root screens (Bible, Saved, Settings); collapse it to the centred 17px title once the content scrolls.
Use the back ‹ variant on any screen reached by drilling in (a chapter, a setting).
Use search mode when the reader taps the search field; it replaces the whole bar until Cancel.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it on websites; use SiteHeader there.

anatomy.description:
Status bar `.ap-sb` (40px) + `.ap-bar` row (56px). Inside a phone frame use `.ap-screen`; for isolated specimens use `.ap-iso`. Large title: `.ap-bar.ap-bar-end` (actions only) + `

Bible

` + `.ap-px` wrapping an `.ap-field` search field.

props.name: variant
props.description: `standard` is the 56px row, `large` adds a 32px title (and optional search field) for root screens, `search` replaces the bar with a search field and Cancel.

props.name: title
props.description: Screen title that names the place ("Bible", "John 3"). One line, under 20 characters.

props.name: back
props.description: Back button: shows ‹ plus the parent screen name, never "Back". Used on drilled-in screens.

props.name: actions
props.description: Trailing icon actions, at most three (extras are dropped; move them into More). Primary first, More last.

props.name: scrolled
props.description: Collapsed state after scroll: glass white with a hairline, centred title.

props.name: dark
props.description: Dark reader surface (`.ap-dark`).

props.name: glass
props.description: Use translucent glass action buttons for placing the bar over imagery (add your own scrim).

props.name: statusBar

whenToUse: Use it on long pages: articles, stories, the Statement of Faith, policy pages, the resource library.

whenToUse: Any form with more than about five fields or two topics: Become a church partner, Broadcast partner application, publishing and NFC card orders.

components.name: Loader
components.title: Loader
components.summary: Spinners for short waits, a busy state for buttons, and shimmering skeletons that hold the shape of content while it loads.
whenToUse: Use a spinner for a wait under about 2 seconds inside a control or a small area: sending a form, loading a menu.
Use the button loading state after a submit: Give, Send, Save.
Use skeletons when a page or list of content is loading: cards, list rows, a chapter of text.
Use Progress instead when you know how far along the work is (downloads, uploads, steps).
whenNotToUse: Do not show a full-page spinner. Show the page frame and skeletons for the parts still loading.

props.name: tone

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name; say what is loading, for example "Loading stations".

props.description: 16, 24 or 40dp. S in buttons and inputs, M in menus and cards, L in an empty panel.

props.description: Hide from screen readers when the surrounding control already says it is busy (e.g. inside a Button).

rules: Spinner turns once every 0.8s. Never colour a spinner with a status colour.
Pick the size by context: S inside buttons and inputs, M inside menus and cards, L in an empty panel.
A loading button keeps its width (set `min-width` to its idle width), shows the spinner before the verb, and cannot be clicked again (`.fb-busy`).
Change only the clicked button; leave the rest of the group as is.
Skeleton shimmer runs `--gray-100` to `--gray-200` over 1.4s. Lines are 12px tall with 6px radius; media blocks use `--radius-md`.
Shape skeletons like the real layout: same card size, same row height, same number of lines (roughly).
Show a skeleton only after 300ms; if content arrives sooner, show nothing.
Replace skeletons with the content in one swap; never fade each line separately.
If loading fails, replace the loader with an EmptyState offline or error panel.

components.name: Logos
components.title: Logos
components.summary: The ISM and dot.Bible logos, marks and brand patterns, with the rules for placing them on light and dark surfaces.
whenToUse: Use the **ISM full logo** in the site header, footer, print covers and email headers.
Use the **ISM mark** where space is tight: favicons, avatars, app tiles for ISM itself, social profile images.
Use the **dot.Bible full logo** wherever the dot.Bible app is the subject (app banners, store pages, app promos). Use the **dot.Bible icon** for the app tile and small placements.
Use the **patterns** (Circle-symbol-1, Dots 1–5) as quiet background texture on campaign, print and hero art. Never behind body text.
whenNotToUse: Do not redraw, recolour, stretch, outline or add effects to any logo.

anatomy.description: All logo files are drawn in black ink. On dark surfaces invert them with a filter; do not use the "White" files (they render black). CSS custom properties for the files ship in `tokens/logos.css`: `--logo-full-black`, `--logo-mark-black`, `--logo-dotbible-full-black`, `--logo-dotbible-mark-black` (use with `background-image` / `mask-image`).

whenToUse: Use a dialog (S or M) for a short focused task that should not leave the page: send an app link, request NFC Bible cards.
Use the confirmation dialog before an action that cannot be undone or loses work: remove a partner, leave an unfinished sign-up.
whenNotToUse: Do not use a modal for long forms, reading content or anything with more than one step; give it its own page.
Do not open a modal on page load or on scroll. Open it only from a click.
Do not confirm actions that can be undone; do them and offer Undo in a Toast.

rules: Scrim `rgba(22,24,25,.6)` (charcoal-900 at 60%). Panel `--white`, radius `--radius-lg`, shadow `--shadow-overlay`.

Lock page scroll while open. One modal at a time; never open a modal from a modal.

components.name: Pagination
components.title: Pagination
components.summary: Moves through a long list split into pages (news, resources, partner lists): numbered pages with Previous / Next, a compact "Page 3 of 12" form, or a Load more button.
whenToUse: Use numbered pagination for lists people browse and return to, where the URL should hold the page: news, stories, the resource library.
Use compact pagination on phones and in tight spaces such as cards and side panels.
Use Load more for feeds people scan once, such as partner stories or radio episodes.
whenNotToUse: Do not paginate lists under about 12 items; show them all.

props.description: Total number of pages.

props.description: `numbered` shows page buttons with Previous / Next; `compact` shows round arrows around "Page 3 of 12".

props.description: Builds the URL of a page. Use real `?page=` URLs so pages can be shared.

props.description:
Called when a page link is clicked, with the target page and the click event.
Call `event.preventDefault()` for client-side paging without a navigation.

props.description:
Component used to render page links. Defaults to `'a'`.
Pass `next/link` (or any component accepting `href`, `className`, `onClick`, `aria-*` and `children`).

props.description: Accessible name of the `<nav>`.

props.description: Accessible name of the round Previous arrow (compact).

Renders the compact status ("Page 3 of 12", current number bold). Receives the page and the count.

variantNotes: **Page button (`.nv-pg-btn`):** 44px round, 15px/500 `var(--charcoal-900)`. Hover `var(--gray-100)`. Focus: blue outline + `var(--shadow-focus)`. Current: filled `var(--charcoal-900)`, white 600, `aria-current="page"`.
**Gap (`.nv-pg-gap`):** an `…` that is not clickable.
**Previous / Next (`.nv-pg-nav`):** outlined 44px pills with arrows. At the ends: `aria-disabled="true"` (opacity .45, not clickable).
**First page:** Previous disabled; show 1 2 3 … 12.

props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible `label`.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value from 0 to `max`. Ignored when `indeterminate`.

props.name: max
props.description: Total.

components.summary: Grouped inset settings for ISM apps: section headers, inset cards of 52px rows with toggles, values with ›, radio choices, a separate Sign out card and helper text.
whenToUse: Use on Settings and preference screens in dot.Bible and other ISM apps.
Use a toggle row for an on/off setting that applies at once.
Use a value row with › when the choice opens another screen (Language, Translation).
Use radio rows for picking one of two to five options in place (Default Bible).
whenNotToUse: Do not use these rows for content lists such as search results or episodes; use SearchResults or ListRow.

components.name: SiteHeader

components.summary: The site-wide black header bar for ism.bible: ISM mark, five main links (three open submenus), a white Give pill and a menu button that opens the mobile drawer.
whenToUse: Use it once, at the top of every ism.bible page and every page built from the website kit.
whenNotToUse: Do not use it inside apps (dot.Bible app screens have their own top bar) or in email.

react.notes: `import { SiteHeader } from '@ism/ui'` (source: `packages/react/src/components/SiteHeader.tsx`). Data-driven: it renders the bar and drawer markup below from `navigation`, and handles the behaviour in Accessibility: submenus open on click and mouse hover and close on Esc (focus returns to the caret button) and outside click. The drawer traps focus, closes on Esc and scrim click, locks body scroll and returns focus to the menu button. `.is-scrolled` is added automatically past 8px. Only `navigation` is required. Give, the drawer buttons and the skip link are not built in; pass them as props.

variantNotes: **Top of page:** `.hdr` with a transparent bottom border.
**Scrolled (>8px):** add `.is-scrolled` for the shadow and white hairline.
**Current section:** `aria-current="page"` on the link or caret button shows the gradient underline.
**Submenu open:** caret button `aria-expanded="true"`, caret rotates 180°, `.nv-subpanel` drops 14px below the bar. Row hover is `rgba(255,255,255,.07)`.
**Below 1024px:** `.ism-desk` hides the links; the menu button opens the drawer. Caret rows (`.nv-dparent`) expand in place, one at a time; open row turns `var(--blue-on-dark)`.
**Static preview:** add `.nv-static` to `.hdr` or `.drawer` to drop fixed positioning (docs and boards only).

components.name: SkipLink
components.title: SkipLink
components.summary: The first focusable element on every page: an off-screen "Skip to content" link that appears as a white pill over the header on the first Tab press and jumps keyboard users past the navigation.
whenToUse: Use it on every ism.bible page and every page built from the website kit, as the first element in `body`.
Use it in web apps with a repeated header or side navigation.
whenNotToUse: Do not hide it permanently or remove it because "nobody sees it". Keyboard and screen reader users rely on it.

anatomy.description: `.skip` (shared layer) keeps it off-screen at `left:-9999px`. `.nv-skip` sets the website look: 15px/600 black text on a white pill, 12px from the top. On focus it moves to `left:16px` and shows the focus ring.

props.name: children
props.description: Visible text, which is also the accessible name. Translate it per site language, for example "Skip to content".

props.name: href
props.description: Fragment link to the main landmark. The target should be `<main id="main" tabIndex={-1}>`.

variantNotes: **Hidden (page load):** off-screen, still first in the tab order.
**Focused (first Tab):** white pill at top-left 16px over the black header, 2px `var(--horizon-blue)` outline, 2px offset, `var(--shadow-focus)`. `.nv-shown` forces this for docs.
**Activated:** the page scrolls to `main`, and focus moves to `main[tabindex="-1"]`. The link hides again when it loses focus.

states.universal: See rules/states.md for the seven required states and their hooks.

rules: Make it the very first focusable element, before the header, cookie banner and any app banner.
Point it at `#main` and give `main` `tabindex="-1"` so focus actually moves.
Keep it above everything (`z-index:100`) so it is never hidden under the fixed header.
Hide it with off-screen positioning, never with `display:none` or `visibility:hidden` (that removes it from the tab order).
Keep the white pill on the black header; never colour it Horizon Blue.
One skip link per page. Add a second ("Skip to search") only in apps with a large side navigation.
Keep its height at least 44px including padding on touch devices.

whenToUse: Use on ISM Radio and Global Bible Network pages to list partner and HD Radio stations.
Use in a grid of 2–4 cards, or one card beside a NetworkMap selection.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for audio Bible chapters; use AudioPlayer.
Do not use for a partner organisation without a station; use PartnerCard.

components.name: Tooltip
components.title: Tooltip
components.summary: A small dark label that names an icon-only control on hover or focus, and its light popover sibling that opens on click to explain something with a title and one link.
whenToUse: Use a tooltip on every icon-only button that has no visible text: Copy link, Share verse, Listen, Save verse.
Use a popover for a short explanation next to a control or term, such as what offline reading needs.
whenNotToUse: Do not put essential information only in a tooltip; touch screens may never show it.
Do not put links, buttons or anything interactive in a tooltip. Use a popover.
Do not use a popover for a task with inputs; use a Modal.

anatomy.description: Tooltip: trigger (`position: relative`) + `.fb-tip` + side class. Popover: trigger with `aria-expanded` + `.fb-pop` with title, body and optional link.

props.name: children
props.description:
The trigger: one element, usually an icon-only `<button className="fb-ib" aria-label="Copy link">`.
It must be `position: relative` (`.fb-ib` is). The tooltip is rendered inside it, as in the README markup.

props.name: label
props.description: Two or three words, sentence case, verb first, no full stop. Never put interactive content here.

props.name: side
props.description: Preferred side. Defaults to top; use `bottom` under a header.

props.name: delay
props.description: Hover delay in ms before the tooltip shows. Keyboard focus shows it immediately.

props.name: className
props.description: Class names for the tooltip bubble.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the tooltip element (used by `aria-describedby`). Generated when omitted.

variants.notes: default
when there is no room above (e.g. under the header)
for controls at a screen edge or in a vertical rail

rules: Tooltip: `--charcoal-900` fill, white 13px/500 text, radius `--radius-sm`, padding 7px 10px, 10px gap to the trigger plus a 10px arrow. One line, no wrap.

Popover: `--white`, 1px `--gray-200` border, radius `--radius-md`, shadow `--shadow-overlay`, padding 16px 18px, max-width `calc(100vw - 32px)`.
Popover title 16px/600, body 14px `--gray-700`, link 14px/600 Horizon Blue.
Link icons: ↗ when the link goes to another page; › when it drills into an app screen.
Popovers open on click, not hover. Esc, a click outside, or the trigger again closes them. Only one open at a time.
Triggers are 44px tap targets and keep the focus ring while their popover is open.

content: Tooltips: two or three words, sentence case, verb first. "Copy link", "Share verse", "Save verse", "Listen".

Popovers: a short title, one or two plain sentences, one link. "Read without a connection. Download a Bible once and it stays on your phone. Audio needs about 600 MB of space." (600 MB is a sample figure.)
No full stops in tooltips. No emoji.

whenToUse: Use `.sx-verse` to feature one verse or a short passage inside a page, article or app screen.

components.name: VideoPlayer
components.title: VideoPlayer
components.summary: A 16:9 video frame: a poster with a large white play button, caption and duration chips, and while playing a bottom control bar with seek, time, captions, settings and full screen.
whenToUse: Use for ISM stories, field reports and dot.Bible app explainers on ism.bible.
Use one featured video per section, with a title and summary under it.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for audio-only Scripture; use AudioPlayer.
Do not use as a decorative background loop.
